items.stem: In maintenance management, what is the key difference between planning and scheduling a job?

options.text: Planning defines what work and how; scheduling defines who does it and when
options.rationale: Correct: planning is the scope, method, parts and labour estimate; scheduling assigns it to people and a time.

options.text: Planning assigns the date; scheduling lists the parts
They are the same activity with different names
options.rationale: They are distinct steps with different owners and outputs.
Planning applies mainly to proactive, non-emergency work.

items.explanation: Correct: planning is the scope, method, parts and labour estimate; scheduling assigns it to people and a time.

items.stem: Which TWO situations most justify a predictive (condition-based) strategy over fixed-interval PM? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The failure gives measurable warning signs before it occurs
options.rationale: Correct: a detectable P-F interval is what makes condition monitoring effective.

options.text: The asset is critical and downtime is costly
options.rationale: Correct: higher consequence justifies the cost of monitoring to avoid surprise failure.

options.text: The failure is sudden with no detectable precursor
options.rationale: With no warning signal, condition monitoring cannot give useful lead time.

options.text: The asset is cheap, redundant and low-consequence
options.rationale: Low consequence usually favours run-to-failure, not predictive maintenance.

items.explanation: Correct: a detectable P-F interval is what makes condition monitoring effective.

items.stem: A team completed 18 of 24 scheduled jobs this week. What is the schedule compliance, and what does a persistently low value suggest?

options.text: 75%; the schedule is being broken by reactive work or poor planning
options.rationale: Correct: 18/24 = 75%, and chronic low compliance points to interruptions or unrealistic schedules.

options.text: 75%; the team simply needs to work faster
options.rationale: Low compliance is usually a planning/interruption problem, not effort.
You cannot complete more than were scheduled here; the ratio is 18/24.

options.text: 25%; a quarter of work was done
options.rationale: 25% is the non-completion share, not schedule compliance.

items.explanation: Correct: 18/24 = 75%, and chronic low compliance points to interruptions or unrealistic schedules.
